names.iupac: (−)-(6aR,10aR)-6,6,9-trimethyl-3-pentyl-6a,7,8,10a-tetrahydro-6H-benzo[c]chromen-1-ol (Δ9-THC; the 'fully systematic name' given by EUDA)
cas: 1972-08-3: Δ9-THC, dronabinol (NIST, read twice). The EUDA profile prints '1972-08-03' after its statement that only the (−)-trans isomer occurs naturally (read twice), a misprint: the last part of a CAS number is a single check digit.
synonyms: Delta-9-Tetrahydrocannabinol (delta-9-THC) and its stereochemical variants (INCB listing)

forms.detail: Cannabis sativa L. (EUDA); AIHW names Cannabis sativa and Cannabis indica as subspecies; AIHW: THC is the main psychoactive component of the plant.

Cannabidiol (WHO ATC N03AX24). CAS 13956-29-1, formula C21H30O2 and molar mass 314.4617 (NIST, read twice); NIST other names include (−)-trans-cannabidiol and CBD. EUDA names CBD but gives no identifiers.
EUDA: the dried flowering tops and leaves; AIHW: herbal cannabis, also referred to as marijuana; DEA: a dry, shredded green/brown mix of flowers, stems, seeds and leaves.
EUDA: a compressed solid made from the resinous parts of the plant; AIHW: the dried resin from the cannabis plant; DEA shows 'hash or hashish'.
EUDA: a solvent extract of cannabis, a dark viscous liquid; AIHW: the oil extracted from the resin.

AIHW: medicinal products that contain THC or CBD, including pharmaceutical CBD/THC oil (Australia). EUDA mentions cannabis flos (prescription herbal cannabis in the Netherlands), the Sativex extract and dronabinol as a licensed medicine in some countries.
